items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: The interviewee discusses Milt Jackson extensively as a friend, but Mona is only mentioned by the interviewer in the context of being Milt's wife and being well-regarded by the public. The interviewee's response ('They are good people') refers to both, but no direct personal interaction or specific

ctx.x: Yeah, 86 or 87. His wife’s not too well. She has got some problems, but they are the nicest people, and I can’t think of one nasty or even off thing about Milt, ever. He’s always been a gentleman to everybody, kind, generous to a fault. I can go by asking myself, if I called him and said, “Milt you’ve got to do this thing for me because I need you for such-and-such like that, and I can’t pay you anything,” he’d say okay. Fortunately it didn’t happen very often, but, and he would take off from someplace else to do…

Well you can measure I think how they’re, Milt and Mona are looked upon by when you see them at a festival or something, they can’t even get down the hall because so many people just want to be around them.
They are good people. They really are good people. All over the world he’s known. Somebody told me that he’s getting better.
